description: Kotlin Multiplatform client for the Spider transit API — trip planning, stop departures, and single-trip lookups from one typed, coroutine-based client on JVM, Android, iOS, JS, and Wasm.
rules: Create the client with `SpiderClient(baseUrl = "https://your-env-slug.api.tiducto.eu", apiKey = "your-api-key")`; the dependency is `eu.tiducto:spider-sdk-kotlin-client` on Maven Central. The base URL is per-environment and the key travels in the `apikey` header — always use the literal placeholders `your-env-slug` and `your-api-key`, never a real slug or key. All three surfaces (`client.routing`, `client.stops`, `client.realtime`) are available immediately; there is no install or registration step.

Every call is a `suspend` function returning `SpiderResult<T>`; branch on it instead of catching exceptions: `when (val r = client.routing.plan(origin, destination)) { is SpiderResult.Success -> r.data; is SpiderResult.Error -> r.error }`. A `SpiderResult.Error` wraps a `SpiderError` whose `code` is one of network, timeout, unauthorized, not_found, server, rate_limited, decoding, or unknown.

Routing has three operations on `client.routing`: `plan(origin, destination, ...)` returns a `Route` of itinerary edges (page with `planNext(route)` / `planPrevious(route)`), `departures(stopId)` lists upcoming departures for a stop, and `trip(tripId)` returns one trip's stops and times. Build an origin or destination with `Location.Stop(gtfsId)` or `Location.Coordinate(lat, lon)`; ids are opaque and feed straight from one call into the next — never re-prefix them.

`client.stops.search { filter { name eq "..." } }` does text and geographic stop search (plus `byId`, `near`, `within`), and `client.realtime` is poll-based with no push or streaming — `vehicles`, `vehicleForTrip`, `delays`, and `alerts`, each result carrying a `FeedFreshness`. Tune retry per surface inside the constructor block, e.g. `SpiderClient(baseUrl, apiKey) { realtime { autoRetry { maxAttempts = 3 } } }`.
